hunts.label: Saturday, Oct 31
hunts.subtitle: Halloween dawn: cool, still, and the only thing you want to hear is a leaf that does not belong.

rules.title: Clocks fall back after this hunt
items: Clocks go back one hour at **2:00 am Sunday, Nov 1**. Saturday morning is still daylight time. Every time on this page is the clock you will see Saturday.
Sunday sunrise will be near 6:30 am and legal light near 6:00 am on the new clock.
Hunter orange is required for firearm hunters (Oct 17 to Jan 1). Hat and vest on.
rules.note: Set your alarm for Saturday only. Check that your phone shows the right time Sunday morning.

conditions.source: Source: National Weather Service point forecast, updated 3:23 pm Friday. Sun times from sunrise-sunset.org.
items: **Walk-in, 5:45 am:** about 51°F. Mostly clear. North wind near 5 mph.
**9 am:** about 52°F. North wind 7 mph, turning northeast and rising to 9 or 10 mph by midday. High near 63°F.
**Precipitation:** none (0% all morning). Humidity 74 to 83%, so expect damp leaves.
**Moon:** waning gibbous, about 58% lit at the end of the day.
conditions.meaning: **What it likely means (my assumption, not proven):** a steady north breeze and a cool clear dawn favor deer moving early, 6:59 to 8:00, with a second push as it warms near 9. Damp leaves are quieter than dry ones, which helps you walk in. A north wind carries your scent south, behind you, away from the swamp and the woods to the north.
conditions.hours_note: No gusts forecast. Precipitation chance is 0% for every hour. Coldest point is about 7 am.

wind.label: from the N, light, about 5 mph, rising to 7 by 9 am

in_season: **Deer, either sex** (gun season, day 15). Pre-rut: bucks are starting to cruise.

in_season.tip: Needs your HIP number and the 3-shell plug. Confirm the shot rule in the Digest before you shoot one. If unsure, just look.
Opportunity only. Take one only if it commits over your sit and the backstop is safe.

in_season.text: Awareness only: rails, gallinules, bobcat and bear
in_season.tip: Rails are open but the swamp is poor habitat. Bobcat is open. Bear is closed until Nov 14. You are not hunting these. Slugs are for defense only.

in_season: Ducks and dove are closed today. Both reopen Nov 7. Woodcock is not planned for today.

plan.title: The plan: the Lower Pines funnel, on a north wind
plan.why: **Why here:** a north wind is the cleanest wind you have had. Sit on the main trail about halfway between the yard and the Junction, in the tallest pines, 30 yards EAST of the trail, facing N and NE. Your scent drifts south and west, away from the swamp and away from deer coming down from the north. You have not sat this stretch yet, so it also teaches you the land. **Timing:** legal light is 6:59. You want to be seated about 45 minutes before, around 6:15. The walk is short, so leave the yard at 5:45, not 4:30. A long wait in the cold only makes you fidget.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail, heading NE. Red light low. Three steps, listen, three steps. Damp leaves help you.
Find the funnel: the stretch where tall pines crowd the main trail and a holly thicket sits to the west. Step off the trail 30 yards to the EAST. Pick a trunk wider than your shoulders.
Sit with your back to the trunk. Face N and NE. Check what is behind every lane before you load. No house, no field, nothing south or southwest.
Load at the sit, muzzle pointing N. Safety on. Tie a 12-inch thread to the barrel to see the real wind.
Legal light. Watch the north and northeast first, then the trail. Look for ears, legs and a flicking tail, not whole deer.
No deer? Stay. Count to 100 slowly twice before you move. The warming air may start a second push.
Swap 00 for #4. Walk the loop trail, east then north, for squirrel and rabbit. Shoot N, NE, E or W only.
Practice the carry-out route (see the Skill tab) as you walk back toward the yard.
Unload at the yard edge. Log what you saw with a "note:" message.

items: **In the gun:** 00 buckshot in the magazine. Modified choke. Safety on.
**Right pocket:** #4 and #7.5 birdshot. Swap in at about 8:30.
**Also carry:** knife, hatchet, gloves, 12-inch thread, 10 feet of cord, dry layer, cushion.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot.
Never shoot buckshot or slugs without the ground behind the target.
Keep buckshot and birdshot in different pockets. Check by feel.

animals.name: Deer
paragraphs: **Local:** common. They bed in the swamp thickets and feed toward the pasture side and the mast trees.
**Today:** pre-rut with a cool north breeze. Best window (assumption): 6:59 to 8:00, then 8:30 to 9:00.
**Shot:** broadside or quartering away only. 30 yards maximum with 00. Aim behind the front shoulder, middle of the body. Shoot only N, NE, E or W. Never south.

details.title: Technique: let the woods tell you
steps: Squirrels and jays scold at a walking deer or a hawk. A sudden scolding from one direction means look there slowly.
A sudden silence in birds near you means something is moving. Stop moving and scan.
Move only your eyes first, then your head over 10 seconds.
If a deer is walking, shoot only when it pauses with a good angle.
details.note: A scolding squirrel that faces away from you is looking at something else. Follow its line of sight.

after: **Tip:** check the thread at 6:15 and 8:15. If the wind swings to come from the east or west, your scent now drifts toward the lanes, so hold still and be ready to shift.
**Tip:** report any harvest as the NCWRC Regulations Digest requires.

animals.name: Squirrel
paragraphs: **Local:** gray squirrels are seen often. Fox squirrel is possible.
**Today:** damp leaves and a cool dawn. After 8:30 the sun warms the east-facing trunks and squirrels come down to feed. (Assumption.)
**Shot:** head and neck. #4 to 30 yards. #7.5 to 25 yards.

details.title: Technique: freeze after the alarm
steps: If a squirrel spots you and barks, freeze against a trunk.
Stay still 10 minutes with your gun low.
Curiosity brings it back. It often returns to the same limb.
Shoot only with a trunk or the ground behind it. Never toward the house.

after: **Tip:** look for piles of cut nut husks at a trunk base. That is a feeding tree. Mark it for next week.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: **Local:** likely at the feed bins and along thick edges.
**Shot:** #4 to 30 yards, N, NE, E or W only.

details.title: Technique: the stop-and-wait edge walk
steps: Walk the thick edge into the low sun. Take three steps, stop for ten seconds.
A rabbit sitting tight gets nervous when you pause close by and often bolts.
Look for a dark eye and the shape of an ear, low in the grass.
Shoot when it is clear of cover and has stopped, not while it zigzags.

after: **Safety:** wear gloves when you handle it. Check the liver for spots.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Opportunity only. A dawn return to a den near the bins is possible. Same shot rules. Never toward the house or field.

animals.name: Snipe
paragraphs: **Local:** possible on soft mud near the beaver lodge. A low-odds extra.
**Rule:** needs your HIP number and the 3-shell plug. Confirm the shot rule in the Digest first. If you cannot confirm it, skip the shot.

details.title: Technique: look before you walk
steps: Scan wet mud from the edge for a long bill probing.
Snipe burst up with a raspy call and zigzag.
Do not shoot toward the south.

after: **Tip:** check only on the walk out after 8:30.

animals.name: Crow
paragraphs: **Local:** common flyers over the pasture and swamp. Saturday is an open day.
**Today:** opportunity only. Stay still against your trunk and shoot only a bird that commits close overhead with a safe backstop.

skill.title: Skill of the week: plan the carry-out before you ever shoot
skill.principle: **Core principle:** a deer is heavy and the warm hours are short. Decide the drag route and what you carry before the shot. It is the same as sign reading: use the land you already know.

sections.title: Plan the route (do this today)
steps: From your sit, walk the easiest path to the main trail. Count the steps.
Note any ditch, fallen log, or thick brush on that path. Pick a way around.
Downhill is easier. The land slopes toward the swamp, so a drag toward the yard is uphill. Plan rests every 50 yards.
Cut about 10 feet of cord now and keep it in your pocket. Tie it around the front legs or the neck for a head-first drag.
Always drag head first, antlers or neck toward you. The hair lies flat and the body slides.

sections.title: After the shot (read this once)
steps: Wait with the gun down for 30 minutes. Mark the spot where the deer stood.
Follow the blood trail from last week's Skill tab. Do not rush.
Field dress it first (see the earlier Skill tab). Start cooling the meat within one hour.
Check the Digest for how and when to report the harvest.

details.title: Tap to open: why plan before the shot
paragraphs: Excited hunters forget details. If the route is already in your head, you can focus on the meat. In warm weather, hours matter. Walking the route once today, without a deer, costs nothing.

skill.checkpoint: **Checkpoint:** on the walk out, count how many steps it is from your sit to the yard. Send it in a "note:" message.

land.intro: Learn the Lower Pines stretch of the main trail. Make notes on the walk out.
steps: Count your steps from the yard to your sit tree, and from the sit to the Junction.
Look for deer tracks crossing the main trail near your sit. Note which way they point.
Look at the ground under any big tree for cut husks, shells, or droppings. Note which trees.
Run the thread test at 6:15 and 8:15. Write down which way it points.
Send a "note:" message with what you found. Next week's plan will use it.

safety: **Shooting arc:** north and northeast. Never beyond east or west. NEVER south. The house is SW, the field is SE, the neighbor is south.
Buckshot and slugs need the ground behind them.
Hunter orange on. Hat and vest.
Cool at dawn, about 50°F. Bring a dry layer and gloves. Do not let numb hands handle the gun.
Walk in the dark with the red light. Watch for roots, holes and stumps.
Bear and fox are in the area. Slugs are for defense only.
hunts.regs: Check the NCWRC Regulations Digest for deer reporting, bag limits, snipe and crow rules.
hunts.gaps: no hunting entries in your Daily Notes this week. I could not find Saturday moonrise or moonset times. I could not confirm the shot-type rule for snipe or the woodcock dates, so those are marked check-first.
